items.notes: Chapter landing on messaging families and delivery contracts; contextual only, no late-message disposition. Event-time stream processing context (late/out-of-order events), not resequencer gap disposition. Stock-and-flow modeling is unrelated to message ordering. Messaging-family selection page; does not address messages arriving after a resequencer gap.

Outbox/inbox chapter overview; no poison-row or relay-stall procedure. Outbox publication research; adjacent failure context but no poison-row plan. Outbox publication and ordering mechanism; does not address a poison row stalling the relay. Saga compensation is unrelated to a stuck outbox relay.

Combined caching research covers invalidation and overload, but not synchronized expiry specifically. Directly about stampedes and source protection after synchronized expiry. Chapter on cache invalidation, stampedes and hot keys; directly covers the burst mechanism. Edge-cache origin recovery is adjacent; not the short-TTL expiry explanation.

Cache authority and freshness design; not the transient stale-read window after invalidation. Combined cache invalidation research; adjacent but not focused on post-write reads. Cache-aside and refresh races directly explain transient stale reads after invalidation. Stale fills and regeneration ownership directly address obsolete values after refresh.

Static content hosting page; owns the fit and limits of dedicated static hosting. Edge-delivery chapter landing; static hosting is one section, not the answer. Compute models are unrelated to static content personalization. Scaling models are unrelated to static content hosting.

Directly asks which representation an edge may reuse and how correctness is preserved. Explicitly lists host-owned upload validation, origin protection and prewarming. Gateway offloading is a different responsibility from edge static-content hosting. API and service communication chapter landing; unrelated.

Transition-state chapter context; no cutover verification checklist in the excerpt. Decision playbook on compatibility, shadow differences and authoritative cutover. Reader/writer compatibility supports migration planning but not the authority switch gate. Disaster-recovery contracts do not cover migration cutover verification.

Throughput and scaling laws, not implementation comparison overhead. Cutover case using shadow validation; related but not framed as a lower-overhead comparison alternative. Service extraction context; parallel-run alternatives are not shown in the excerpt. Invariants and executable models are a plausible verification alternative, but the page is not about migrations.

Directly covers authoritative audit and the integrity the actor must not control. Distinguishes logs, audit and lineage records; supports audit authority. Logging/audit chapter landing; contextual only. Collection privacy and retention for agent-accessible services; not audit tampering.

Incident exercise readiness; not liveness-probe semantics. Discovery and load balancing; not health-probe design. Failure-domain placement; not why a dependency outage should not restart a healthy process. Recovery hysteresis supports why premature restarts hurt, but not liveness-probe design.
